📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:00 EST, 15 November 2026.

Clive Tyldesley reaches for his glasses as he rummages through the commentary charts crammed into an old filing cabinet, jokes about his fading eyesight and supposes one day he will no longer be able to identify footballers from the gantry.

Recent findings suggest that fortunately, we are still far from that point. At 72, Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever. His eyes are perfectly good when bespectacled, his mind nimble enough to keep up with play and his soothingly familiar voice strong and authoritative with a gentle tendency towards self-deprecation.

This much was evident as Manchester United roared back to beat Roma in the Champions League and a clip of his spine-tingling commentary from the live CBS broadcast circulated on social media and found an appreciative audience in Europe.

According to recent reports, 'I don't know if there's an element of nostalgia in hearing my voice again,' says Tyldesley. 'If I'm honest, I've dodged the worst of the public's ire with everything including commentators because I haven't been around for the last few years.

It has been revealed that 'Absence has made a few hearts grow a little fonder towards me and maybe if I'd been on Sky every week for the last six years, I'd be no less unpopular than anybody else out there. So, I can't pretend it's not nice to get some engagement with an audience I used to commentate to on a regular basis, but I'm very happy where I am.'.

Tyldesley has been the lead commentator for the CBS coverage of the Champions League since 2020, converting transfer fees into US dollars and keeping his measurements imperial for a North American audience but otherwise approaching the job as he always did.

Clive Tyldesley is calling the game as accurately as ever at 72 and is 'very happy' in his role as the lead commentator of CBS coverage of the Champions League.

Tyldesley's commentary of Man United's comeback against Roma circulated on social media and received an appreciative audience in Europe.

The 72-year-old wonders whether there was an element of nostalgia to the reaction, with Tyldesley's work for CBS meaning his commentary cannot be shown in Europe.

Clips of the studio panel featuring Thierry Henry, Micah Richards, Jamie Carragher and presenter Kate Scott are popular on social media but live action featuring Tyldesley's commentary is governed by broadcasting rights deals and cannot be shown in Europe.

The one from Old Trafford of Matheus Cunha's winning goal in the 86th minute slipped through the net on X and reminded everyone his passion for football is undimmed, and his voice can still stand hairs on attention.

According to recent reports, 'I don't think I've seen a better game than the first leg of the Paris Saint-Germain v Bayern Munich Champions League semi-final,' indicates Tyldesley on the rare quality of Europe's elite competition. 'I listened to people with hundreds more England caps than me saying it was bad defending, but I watched the whole game back the next day and it wasn't.

In a recent development, 'I'm sorry but it was wonderful attacking and a show of intent by two coaches who trusted defenders to defend one-on-one and attackers to score more than the opposition. Rob Green was my co-commentator and at the end we just put our microphones down and looked at each other and said, "Wow.".

'I've not forgotten muddy pitches and assassin centre backs. You only need to look on YouTube to see football was different, but you can't pretend it was better. I see terrible games today just as I did then, but particularly in the Champions League, I regularly stumble upon football that gets me off my seat.'.

His exit from ITV, first displaced by Sam Matterface as lead commentator in 2020 and then released entirely after Euro 2024 clearly smarted but Tyldesley is comfortable as the veteran in the fast-changing media landscape.

It has been revealed that 'Most of the principles I picked up from watching John Motson, Barry Davies and Brian Moore in their pomp are applicable to commentary in 2026,' he says. 'There's no need to reinvent that particular wheel.

Recent findings suggest that 'You can offer alternatives such as fan zones and screaming watchalongs for people to view it in a different way. I make it my business to look at J_Tekkz or LDN Movements or whatever is pulling in millions on YouTube.

Tyldesley believes he has not seen a better game than the first leg of PSG's Champions League semi-final with Bayern Munich last year.

The veteran commentator believes most of the principles he learned starting out still apply, but admits to having watched popular new voices to see if anything could apply to his commentary.

Tyldesley also works as a guest lecturer and commentates for blockbuster computer games, as well as selling framed prints of his commentary charts.

'I sample a bit of Mark Goldbridge to see why he's prominent but I'm hearing nothing in those guys applicable to the way I call a football match so I carry on with the same focus I've always had on what constitutes good commentary.'.

The central principle being that the game is bigger than the individuals in it, he points out, with viewers tuning in for the football not the commentator.

'The biggest challenge for a television commentator is to find the right words at the big moments, to go beyond "amazing," "brilliant", "incredible" and try to add some editorial context,' says Tyldesley.

In a recent development, 'Every goal is unique. The words following a goal that is going to be remembered for years should be unique and specific to that goal, but that's difficult to do. It's unscripted performance and difficult to master and capture.

In a recent development, 'I am concentrating hardest for the 10-15 seconds after a significant goal because I'm searching for words which will become a small part of people's memories. That's very different to consciously trying to provide 45-second soundbites to amplify one's own personality and standing on social media.

'There's a danger of media leaning that way as it develops such an emphasis on the bitesize.'.

Among other things, Tyldesley is a guest lecturer for media students at the University of Salford, still doing commentaries for blockbuster computer games and selling framed prints of his commentary charts, something that started as 'a silly idea in lockdown'.

Recent findings suggest that his wife Susan bought a dozen frames to see how it went. Originally, he offered three Champions League finals won by English clubs in 1999, 2005 and 2012. He sent one each to Gary Neville who played for Manchester United in 1999 and Jamie Carragher who played for Liverpool in 2005. They both posted images online and demand skyrocketed.

Recent findings suggest that 'Two good friends,' smiles Tyldesley. 'I probably got about half a million pounds of free advertising out of them.' Sales have soared beyond 50,000. There's a Celtic chart on the gym in Rod Stewart's house. Ant and Dec have bought signed Newcastle charts.

His own venture into podcasting was short-lived and he politely declines between five and ten invitations each week to appear on others.

'I've tried to step back from that kind of thing,' notes Tyldesley. 'So much content I hear on football is empty, verbose and repetitive. Really, there are only so many things you can say about Alexander Isak having his shirt pulled in mid-air and Gary Neville probably mentioned most of them in the 30 seconds following the incident.

Tyldesley has no looks to retire and Paramount, the owners of his employers CBS - and soon to be the owners of TNT Sports - will have the UK rights for the Champions League.

Sales of his framed commentary charts, something that started during lockdown, have soared beyond 50,000.

'There are so many brutally judgmental loud voices in and around football attracting attention that I want to be as far away from as possible, so that's what I do. Unless I sense an opportunity to talk about communication and broadcasting rather than whether club A, B or C should replace their manager. That's not for me Clive.'.

So, there's a little less Tyldesley out there than there was. He was content to stay at home and watch the World Cup from his sofa this summer for the first time since 1990.

Recent findings suggest that but there are no intends to retire. And who knows what might change next season when Paramount, the owners of CBS – and soon to be the owners of current rights holders TNT Sports – have the UK rights for the Champions League.

There might be a familiar voice beamed into our living rooms once again.

When I saw the Dear England play, I was the only person in the theatre who didn't enjoy it, and that was because I hated the portrayal of Harry Kane.

He was written as an uneducated numbskull. Written to laugh at and the theatre laughed at him. He was stupid and gullible, another thick footballer.

And anyone who has spent time with footballers will know they might lack for an Eton College education but are streetwise and invariably smart with a razor sharp sense of humour.

Kane is a leader of those men. There's not a single thing about the person Kane has made himself to laugh or sneer at and I wanted to stand up in the theatre that afternoon and shout at everyone.

Oddly, I was introduced to the playwright James Graham at a function a few weeks later and he kind of pushed me for my opinion of Dear England.

I tried to be diplomatic, but I felt so strongly I ended up scolding him for writing a character called Harry Kane who was nothing like Harry Kane.

In a recent development, so, that was the end of a beautiful friendship before it began. And I'm so thrilled now there's a better appreciation of the person Harry is.

Kocaelispor will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Fenerbahce to Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadium on Saturday evening in the Turkish Super Lig.

Both teams are tied on 19 points from their opening 11 matches, with the hosts seventh in the table, one place below the visitors in sixth, although the Yellow Canaries have scored considerably more goals this season and therefore boast a significantly better goal difference.

Kocaelispor have responded positively to consecutive defeats against Besiktas and Goztepe, going unbeaten in their last three league matches.

Their latest outing produced a 2-0 victory away to Eyupspor, following a goalless draw at home to Caykur Rizespor and a 2-1 victory over Alanyaspor, while they also recorded a 3-0 win over Mazidagi in the Turkish Cup during that run.

Selcuk Inan's side have built their season around a solid defensive foundation, with the hosts having conceded nine goals, a tally bettered only by Trabzonspor (8), giving them the second-best defence in the league, although the Gulf have scored the fewest goals among teams in the top half of the table (13).

Their home form has also been encouraging, with three victories, one draw and one defeat from five league matches at Kocaeli Stadium, where they have scored six goals and conceded just two, although they have failed to win either of their last two home fixtures (D1, L1).

However, Kocaelispor have struggled in this fixture over the years, failing to win any of their last 14 meetings with Fenerbahce, losing nine and drawing five, while they have also lost their last three home encounters.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive in Kocaeli after producing an emphatic response to their recent domestic setbacks, beating Corum 5-0 away from home in their last outing to return to winning ways.

The Yellow Canaries had previously suffered consecutive league defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray, both by 2-1 scorelines, with the latter result particularly damaging as they fell further behind in the title race and prompted Ismail Kartal's resignation.

Emre Belozoglu subsequently took charge and has made an impressive start, recording a 3-2 victory over Liverpool in the Champions League before overseeing the emphatic win against Corum.

Fenerbahce's attack has been particularly productive this season, scoring 29 goals in 11 league matches to give them the most prolific frontline in the division, while their 10 goals conceded also represent the third-best defensive record, although they remain nine points off the top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan introduced the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Industry observers note that things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

In a recent development, with promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

In a recent development, milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Recent findings suggest that milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

It has been revealed that rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

It has been revealed that at times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After the final international break of 2026, Championship action is back on the agenda, with the weekend's round of fixtures ending with one of the division's spiciest encounters.

Indeed, the East Lancashire derby is back for the first time in two seasons, with general Championship observers likely to be tuning into the occasion which matters most to fans of Burnley and Blackburn Rovers.

It has been the Clarets who have enjoyed the majority of recent success in this part of the world, but Rovers fans will now feel it is now their time to receive the limelight.

Blackburn have already caused issues for some of the division's pre-season promotion candidates, but they will also be aware of the fact this is the best opportunity the club has had to get one over on Burnley for many years.

Within the past decade or so, the environment fostered by Burnley's players and supporters, particularly during the Sean Dyche era, made Turf Moor one of the most difficult stadiums for opponents to play at.

Even during the Clarets' recent past, many sides still found it difficult to leave with all three points, with none at all doing so during the 2024/25 season, in which Scott Parker's side conceded just 16 goals.

However, the recent demise in BB10 has been echoed by a newly introduced unwanted record set by the club - the longest period without a home league victory.

Burnley's last success at Turf Moor came on October 18th, 2025, in a 2-0 win over Leeds United, which will have been exactly 400 days by the time Sunday's local feud comes around.

They came agonisingly close to ensuring the record didn't stretch into a 12th month before Mohammed Fuseini's late equaliser for Derby County on September 19th, which prompted this reaction from the 'From the Bee Hole End' podcast.

Sources indicate that "We are now (almost) a year without a win at Turf Moor. That's just incredible.

Rovers are currently positioned nine places and 11 points ahead of Burnley in the table - a feat not many would have predicted in pre-season.

Blackburn have certainly upset the apple cart on occasions this season, having defeated Middlesbrough and West Ham United 2-1 at Ewood Park, whilst also narrowly missing out on a victory by the same scoreline against Wolves at Molineux.

The Blues are only three points behind the play-off places after 15 games as a result, with Andri Gudjohnsen's 10-goal exploits, in particular, key to such a return.

Ahead of this particular grudge match, the squad will know that results on the road must improve if a top-eight bid is to be sustained, having taken just six points from a possible 21.

Whilst the current situation surrounding Fabio Celestini's side, who surrendered a 4-1 lead to lose 5-4 at Cardiff City last time out, will offer plenty of encouragement to those of a Blackburn persuasion, some may be pessimistic due to recent history.

During a period of Clarets-centred dominance in East Lancashire from 2009 to now, Sunday's hosts have not lost in the derby since March 2010, when a David Dunn penalty saw Blackburn achieve a league double over their bitter rivals.

This run stretches back 11 games, with the most high-profile of those coming in April 2023, when Manuel Benson's late curler secured the Championship title at Ewood Park under Vincent Kompany.

It is often debated that players do not need any added incentives to win games of such magnitude, but the news that Tony Mowbray has taken a step back from his role as Blackburn boss for health reasons will only give Rovers' players extra motivation.

They will be led by Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds in the meantime, although both have experience in the dugout on an interim or full-time basis.

Mowbray never took charge of this particular derby in his first spell at Ewood Park, with there even being a two-division gap between the two clubs in 2017/18.

What are your score predictions for Sunday's East Lancashire derby? Comment below!

There could at least be one division separating the two sides in 2027/28 unless fortunes drastically improve, but the chance to pile on further anger at Turf Moor would bring added satisfaction to those making the short trip across the M65.

Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

He may no longer hold top billing outside the club, following a summer in which Chelsea spent a club-record £117m on Morgan Rogers to complete a fearsome front three alongside Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

A giant mural of the Brazilian teenager appeared on the side of a building close to Stamford Bridge in March.

But inside Stamford Bridge, nothing has changed. Estêvão remains one of Chelsea’s star boys and is part of an “untouchable” group of players that also includes Palmer, Rogers and Pedro. Sources believe Estêvão is a player the club will look at rewarding with an improved contract in the coming months.

Having already earned his Chelsea “untouchable” status, the next challenge for the 19-year-old winger – once nicknamed “Messinho” – is to make himself undroppable.

Estêvão may not be a perfect fit for Xabi Alonso’s three-at-the-back formation that features two 10s – Palmer and Rogers – behind a striker. But the boy from Brazil is certainly not being squeezed out and Chelsea’s manager has spoken of the need to be flexible.

According to recent reports, “We are not the favourites to win the Carabao Cup, we know this. Industry observers note that good evening and welcome to live coverage of tonight’s Carabao Cup third-round tie between Chelsea and Leeds United. This is a rematch of last season’s FA Cup semi-final which Chelsea edged by a single Enzo Fernández goal, but plenty has changed since then. Xabi Alonso has taken over the reins at Stamford Bridge and made a promising start, reeling off three wins before losing to Arsenal in an absorbing contest last Sunday. Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, so the domestic cups represent an avenue to silverware, as well as an opportunity to tinker.

In Alonso’s way, though, stands a Leeds team whose manager, Daniel Farke, told the media on Tuesday that his side are aiming to win the Carabao Cup. Farke has overseen an impressive run of form, having lost only two of their previous 16 competitive matches in a stretch that extends back to March. Two wins at Nottingham Forest preceded draws against Brentford and Brighton to keep Leeds undefeated this term. Farke has suggested he will rotate in west London to “integrate new players” having brought in seven new recruits during the summer.

In a recent development, if Leeds are to reach the next round, they must reverse a heavily one-sided head-to-head record against their hosts, who have won each of their past 10 cup meetings (three in the League Cup, seven in the FA Cup). In fact, Chelsea have lost at this stage of the competition just once in the past 15 years, and that was against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City four seasons ago.

Alonso broke up the exhilarating “JP Morgan” band (João Pedro, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers) for Chelsea’s victory over Luton Town in the previous round, handing starts to Danny Welbeck and Estêvão. Players such as Jamie Gittens and Geovany Quenda are also waiting in the wings and may get chances to impress tonight. Mike Penders could also be in line for a start between the sticks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that cardiff City have left the attacker out of their last five squads, despite him being fit and available to play. They are positioned in 14th place in the Championship table after their first 14 fixtures of the season.

In a recent development, robinson, 31, has made seven appearances for the Bluebirds in all competitions in this campaign, six of which have come in the league, and he has chipped in with two goals. However, he hasn’t played for the Welsh side since their home match against Watford in mid-October.

Industry observers note that the Republic of Ireland international, who has 38 caps to his name, is now facing an uncertain long-term future at the Cardiff City Stadium ahead of the January transfer window and his current club will surely look to sell him this winter. He is out of contract at the end of this term and is due to become a free agent in June 2027.

Cardiff City beat Burnley 5-4 in a crazy game last time out before the international break. They will be in confident mood now as they gear up for their upcoming away trip to Norwich City this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that cardiff City risk losing Robinson for nothing when this season ends and he is unlikely to be offered an extension amid his lack of minutes. Therefore, most signs point towards a sale in the near future to ensure that they get a bit of cash for him.

The Northampton-born man has become surplus to requirements with the Bluebirds. He has found it hard to get into Brian Barry-Murphy’s aims ahead of Jack Moylan and Yousef Salach.

Robinson, who rose up through Aston Villa’s academy in his early career, has been with Cardiff City since joining them in 2022. He has since been a good servant and has played 137 games.

Sources indicate that prior to his switch to South Wales, he had a spell at West Brom. He has also featured for the likes of Preston North End and Sheffield United in the past and is experienced in the EFL.

It has been revealed that robinson would benefit from a change of scene away from Cardiff City. Meanwhile, the Bluebirds would free up space and funds to pave the way for other reinforcements.

Sources indicate that he played a key role behind their promotion from League One and found the net on eight occasions. However, he is out of favour now though and a departure seems inevitable.

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026.

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their latest head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Sources indicate that frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington remarked the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'.

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Pfannenstiel mentioned: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager.

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'.

Sources indicate that before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

Recent findings suggest that as a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

It has been revealed that frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and massive ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'.

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48.

Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Genclerbirligi head into Saturday's encounter after suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Besiktas in their last league outing, having been unable to build on the confidence gained from their emphatic 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor a week earlier.

That win was their biggest of the campaign and followed another 5-0 success against Karakopru Belediyespor in the Turkish Cup, but their return to league action in Istanbul brought them back down to earth as Besiktas scored twice before half-time and added a third after the break.

The Red-and-Blacks have now lost three of their last four league matches and won just one of their last nine, with their only victory during that period coming against Alanyaspor, while they have conceded 21 goals in 11 league fixtures, the third-highest total in the division.

Their defensive record has been a particular concern away from home, where they have conceded 14 times in five matches and scored just once, although their performances in Ankara have generally been more encouraging.

Genclerbirligi have collected eight points from six home league matches, winning twice, drawing twice and losing twice, and they have scored nine goals at Eryaman Stadium in the competition, with their 2-1 victory over Fenerbahce representing the highlight.

Bernd Storck's side will hope to avoid another winless streak by bouncing back immediately, with optimism stemming from their home results and the fact that they beat the visitors on this ground in their last meeting here, while they have also never lost to them at home (W4, D1).

Gaziantep, meanwhile, have endured a much more difficult spell, losing their last six league matches and failing to score in each of their most recent two outings.

Their latest defeat came at home against Kasimpasa, who secured a 2-0 victory with both goals coming before the break, while they had previously lost by the same scoreline away to Trabzonspor.

Those results followed defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor, leaving the Red-and-Blacks with just two wins and two draws from their opening 11 matches, alongside seven defeats.

The club subsequently parted company with coach Orhan Ak by mutual agreement following the loss to Kasimpasa, leaving Gaziantep to prepare for this fixture amid another managerial change.

Assistant coach Mustafa Aksoy oversaw the first training session after Ak's departure, but Volkan Demirel has been appointed as their fresh head coach, and the club will be hoping that a change in the dugout can bring an immediate response.

Genclerbirligi will be without Metehan Baltaci, who is suspended after receiving a red card for two yellow cards in the defeat to Besiktas, while Dimitrios Goutas remains sidelined with a serious knee injury that has ruled him out for the season.

Thalisson Kelven is also unavailable through injury, while Kevin Rodrigues remains sidelined and Peter Etebo is a doubt, leaving Storck with decisions to make in defence and midfield.

Pedro Pereira is also doubtful with a muscle injury, while Gokhan Akkan and Muhammet Ensar Cavusoglu are among the other unavailable players.

Gaziantep are expected to be without Kacper Tobiasz, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Nazim Sangare and Fuat Bavuk are also sidelined.

Sontje Hansen is another absentee, leaving the visitors without several options as they look to improve on a difficult run of form.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former QPR striker Charlie Austin believes Julien Stephan’s side must prove their top eight credentials by beating Millwall on Saturday.

It has been a good season for the R’s so far, with the Londoners currently occupying the final play-off spot in the new extended format.

There have been lots of positives for QPR to take in the opening third of the campaign as well, as they’ve been hard to beat, losing just three times, and they have had some very impressive results.

However, there are certainly ways that QPR can improve, and Stephan will want his team to show a ruthless streak as they compete for promotion.

A trip to The Den to take on Millwall on Saturday represents a chance for the R’s to end a five-game winless run on the road.

And, speaking on his Chaz Kicks Off podcast, popular former QPR man Austin cooled talk of Stephan’s side being genuine top two contenders, and he explained why beating a team like Millwall could give the group extra belief as they chase the play-offs.

In a recent development, “Millwall have had a drop off, so the R’s could go there, and it wouldn’t be an upset. It’s way too early to cement yourself (as play-off contenders), but if you want to be taken seriously, of being involved in the play-offs, forget the automatics, then you’ve got to go and take points off teams that are there come May.

According to recent reports, “I expect Millwall to be around it in May, but they’re not hitting the heights of last season. So I expect the R’s to go there all guns blazing.

According to recent reports, “Ilias Chair is back which is a massive boost. You’ve got Charles coming on the back of two fantastic games for Northern Ireland, so for me, I think everything is there to keep momentum going - and I expect them to do that.”.

Even though Millwall have had a difficult campaign so far, most would agree that they are a very good team at this level, as injuries have really impacted their start.

Alex Neil’s side will still fancy their chances of reaching the top eight, but they know they must start to show some consistency, which they haven’t done.

So, QPR will be expecting a difficult game, and it’s fair for Austin to state that this would be a statement win for the R’s if they could head home with all three points.

Millwall did the double over QPR last season, and they also knocked Stephan’s side out of the League Cup back in August.

QPR have won at Portsmouth and Blackburn, who are above Millwall in the table, so Stephan’s side won’t head to The Den with any fear.

But, with the Lions having finished third last season, it’s fair to say that this is a game against an opponent with a lot of quality.

It has been revealed that what is your prediction for Millwall vs QPR? Let us know in the comments below.

Whilst draws at West Brom and West Ham are good in isolation, two heavy defeats at Birmingham and Southampton show that QPR haven’t yet beaten a top team on the road.

So, as Austin says, a statement win could be just what QPR need to give them momentum heading into what is always a pivotal period of the season.

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the latest busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Recent findings suggest that immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Sources indicate that despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Industry observers note that moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

According to recent reports, with four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:30.

Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.

The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.

Galatasaray went into the international break on a six-game winning streak in all competitions, a run that began with a 1-0 victory over Genclerbirligi before they beat Lille 4-2 in the Champions League and Fenerbahce 2-1 at home in the league.

The Lions then won 4-0 away to Konyaspor, beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League and edged Amedspor 4-3 just before the break, with their attacking output particularly impressive as they scored at least twice in five of those six matches.

In the victory over Amed, Galatasaray raced into a 3-0 lead through Rafael Leao's early strike, an own goal from goalkeeper Alban Lafont and Alexey Batrakov's effort before the hour mark, but they subsequently conceded twice before Baris Alper Yilmaz restored their two-goal cushion in the 80th minute, only for the hosts to concede again in stoppage time before holding on for the victory.

Okan Buruk's side have suffered just one league defeat this season, a 4-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, which has left them with 28 points from 11 matches, having also drawn 2-2 at home against Corum in their opening game of the campaign.

Keeping opponents off the scoresheet at home has been an matter for Cimbom, who have conceded in five of their six home league matches this season, including each of their last three.

Samsunspor won the last meeting against Galatasaray to end a nine-game losing streak in this fixture, but the visitors arrive in considerably worse form this season.

However, they received a much-needed boost just before the break, beating Konyaspor 1-0 at home to end an eight-game winless streak, which had been a club record.

It was also the first victory under Nenad Bjelica, who was appointed in October to replace Thorsten Fink, who was dismissed after nine months in charge following just one win in his opening seven matches.

Samsunspor are 17th on seven points, one place above the bottom and one point from safety, and while they finally recorded some positivity before the break, they travel to a venue where they have lost eight consecutive games, leaving them with a difficult task after the international hiatus.

Galatasaray have major absentees, with Victor Osimhen undergoing surgery on a loose fragment in his left knee after the Stuttgart game and expected to be out for several weeks.

Leao is also sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir picked up a shoulder problem on international duty and is not expected to play, with Gunay Guvenc tipped to start between the posts.

Davinson Sanchez is also unavailable after withdrawing from Colombia's squad with a muscle problem, while Roland Sallai is sidelined through injury and Batrakov is also listed as unavailable.

Samsunspor have fewer concerns, although Celil Yuksel is sidelined through injury and Fatih Kaya remains a doubt.

Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the attack, with Tanguy Coulibaly, Oskar Ohlenschlæger and Afonso Sousa providing support from the attacking midfield positions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • QPR right now sit inside the play-off spots in the Championship, and are hoping to replicate some of the magic of Harry Redknapp's 2013/14 team to help bring Premier League football back to Loftus Road.
  • It's been a long time since the R's were last relegated back to the second tier from the top flight, and there hasn't been much to shout about since.
  • It's natural to reminisce over the last piece of success that the club had, and that came in that 2013/14 term, where the Hoops finished fourth in the second tier and prevailed in the play-offs thanks to *that* late Bobby Zamora goal against Derby County.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

QPR right now sit inside the play-off spots in the Championship, and are hoping to replicate some of the magic of Harry Redknapp's 2013/14 team to help bring Premier League football back to Loftus Road.

It's been a long time since the R's were last relegated back to the second tier from the top flight, and there hasn't been much to shout about since. Indeed, this is their 12th consecutive campaign at the level, and they've finished in the bottom half in eight of those 11 seasons.

It's natural to reminisce over the last piece of success that the club had, and that came in that 2013/14 term, where the Hoops finished fourth in the second tier and prevailed in the play-offs thanks to *that* late Bobby Zamora goal against Derby County.

Despite the then-33-year-old taking the plaudits at Wembley, though, it was Charlie Austin's goals which helped power them towards that meeting with the Rams, and his teammates were keen on keeping him fit as the season unravelled.

That QPR squad under Harry Redknapp was filled with veteran heads, from Rob Green in goal to the likes of Zamora and Shaun Wright-Phillips in the frontline. Even a 34-year-old Yossi Benayoun made 16 appearances that year.

Above all those was Richard Dunne, who played out the final couple of years of his career at Loftus Road. The former Manchester City and Ireland international would retire at the end of the 2014/15 campaign, but played 44 times in league and play-off action to help QPR make the Premier League once again.

Dunne was well-regarded as one of the toughest-tackling, bruising defenders in the game in his prime, and speaking on his YouTube channel, Austin, who was 27 at the time, spoke of his time playing alongside him and was thankful he never came up against him.

"Richard Dunne was very, very good, and you wouldn't have liked to play him in his prime, because you wouldn't have gotten much change out of him, that's for sure," he said. "Being tackled by those size elevens with the big studs on...".

His co-host would then interject and ask if he would be on the end of any of those crunching challenges, but Austin, who netted 19 in 34 that year, including both goals in their play-off semi-final win over Wigan Athletic, thankfully stated he was left untouched.

"I was actually alright," he admitted. "They never used to kick me in training. Especially in the Championship, they probably thought, 'If we kick him, who was going to score?'.

"So I was alright; they left me alone.".

The QPR defenders were right to take it a little easier on Austin in their Championship campaign, especially. He was their marquee signing in a summer filled with them, having just netted 24 for Burnley the year before.

The then-27-year-old didn't go the whole campaign injury-free, though. Richard Dunne may not have kicked him in training, but he couldn't stop Austin from picking up a shoulder injury in January 2014 in a win over Bolton Wanderers.

QPR won just four of 12 without Austin in the side, and it was that stint which confined them to the play-offs. He returned just in time, though, netted in the final three games of the year and then more than played his part in the play-offs.

Industry observers note that do you think QPR would have finished in the top two under Harry Redknapp if not for Charlie Austin's injury? Let us know in the comments.

It has been revealed that in the Premier League, he was even better. The 2014/15 campaign was only his first at the level, but he netted 18 in 35, despite QPR's eventual relegation. Only Sergio Aguero, Harry Kane and Diego Costa scored more that season.

He did continue his time at Loftus Road back in the Championship for a little while, but with nine goals in 16, it was evident he was too good for the second tier, and would play into his thirties in the top flight with Southampton.

Industry observers note that julien Stephan's side have been very good to begin the campaign. They sit in the top four in xG difference through 15 games and, in reality, occupy the final play-off spot in the revamped post-season.

Unlike that Harry Redknapp squad, though, the current QPR side are using youth to their advantage, with only Watford, Norwich City and Stoke City fielding an average age lower than the Hoops this year.

Only Glen Kamara is over 30, and the likes of 21-year-old Pierce Charles and 23-year-old's Ronnie Edwards, Harvey Vale and Richard Kone are all key parts of the squad.

Kone is the Charlie Austin of this current squad, the player likely to explode and push towards 20 goals and the player whom their own defenders wouldn't dream of hurting in training this season.

If things can fall into place, QPR can be genuine contenders, and may be looking for some more Wembley success come May.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that west Brom will get the chance to bring in some fresh faces this winter ahead of the second-half of the season.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Baggies were dealt a blow at the start of last month when Noah Galves was ruled out for the rest of the campaign with a serious knee injury.
  • Step forward Ipswich Town defender Darnell Furlong, who could be made available due to a lack of game time at Portman Road following the Tractor Boys’ promotion to the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that west Brom will get the chance to bring in some fresh faces this winter ahead of the second-half of the season. WBA are presently in the Championship play-offs along with Stoke City, Wolves, Swansea City, Southampton and QPR after 15 fixtures.

Recent findings suggest that the Baggies were dealt a blow at the start of last month when Noah Galves was ruled out for the rest of the campaign with a serious knee injury. That has left them short of options at full-back and they would benefit from another option to battle with Brayann Pereira.

Step forward Ipswich Town defender Darnell Furlong, who could be made available due to a lack of game time at Portman Road following the Tractor Boys’ promotion to the Premier League. He was on the books at The Hawthorns from 2019 to 2025 and made 247 appearances in all competitions for the Midlands outfit, chipping in with 11 goals from the back.

West Brom could get the opportunity now to try and lure him back in some capacity. They are back in action this weekend with an away trip to Swansea City.

In a recent development, furlong is under contract at Ipswich Town until June 2028. However, he has slipped down the pecking order in Suffolk and has made only three outings so far this term, one one of which has come in the league.

A change of scene to West Brom would make sense for him. He would be able to get some regular game time under his belt at WBA and help their push for promotion under James Morrison.

Furlong, who is from Luton, knows the club inside out already and is a solid operator in the EFL. He knows what it takes to get out of the second tier and would be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room.

Sources indicate that prior to his switch to the Baggies, he rose up the ranks at QPR and played 72 times for their first-team in his early career. He also had spells away from the Hoops at Northampton Town, Cambridge United and Swindon Town to get some experience under his belt.

Sources indicate that west Brom have been impressive this season but they lack depth. If Pereira got injured, WBA wouldn’t have anyone to play on the right hand side of their backline and would probably have to put Callum Styles there which wouldn’t be ideal.

Recent findings suggest that therefore, they need to consider a swoop for Furlong and it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Ipswich Town sanction a deal, either permanently or on loan. He is surplus to requirements with the Tractor Boys and should seek an exit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:49 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:54 EST, 15 November 2026.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

As he tried to throw the ball out, though, he got it all wrong and ended up launching the ball into his own net.

Bacher, 30, essentially failed to let go of the ball at the right time, leaving his team-mates stunned.

The player himself covered his face with his hand before retrieving the ball to get play started again.

In a recent development, arsenal players wheeled off in celebration, only for Comunicaciones to level things up in the game soon after. Arsenal, though, scored again, and eventually won 3-2 in the first leg of the tie.

"Están matando al fútbol"Por el "insólito" gol en contra que se hace el arquero de Comunicaciones ante Arsenal. pic.twitter.com/GLUJlcKPXK.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored a bizarre own goal during his side's third-tier play-off game.

The 30-year-old failed to release the ball from a throw and debuted the ball into his own net.

Fans flooded to social media to react to the scarcely believable own goal.

One wrote on X: 'Haha, those who think it's because of betting. That's the level of Argentine football.'.

Another posted: 'RIP Argentinian football.'.

A third shared: 'The Arsenal lot celebrating... you've got some nerve.'.

Bacher joined the club at the start of last year, but has always played in his homeland of Argentina.

His Comunicaciones side finished ninth in their league group of Primera B, the third tier of Argentinian football, and were taken on by an Arsenal side that came second.

They will face off in the return leg next Saturday.

Parma vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (662 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12.
  • Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.
  • Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12.

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Despite suffering two agonising Champions League defeats in recent weeks, Roma have hardly faltered on the domestic front; they are one of only two teams still undefeated in Serie A, alongside surprise leaders Lazio.

Soon after swatting Cagliari and Udinese aside, the Giallorossi signed off for the international period with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Sassuolo, in which rising star Rodrigo Mora scored for a third straight league game.

It was an increasingly rare clean sheet for a club boasting the most lethal attack in Italy's top flight: Roma are only the fourth team in 65 years to hit the 30-goal mark by Serie A’s 11th matchday.

Dating back to last term, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored at least twice in all but one of their last 16 league fixtures, only failing to do so in Como, where Donyell Malen was sent off.

Allowed to roam freely into the opposition area, defenders have collectively contributed eight goals this season, easing any pressure on Malen, Mora and their fellow forwards.

Beginning the build-up to next month’s Derby della Capitale, Roma will now seek a fifth straight win over Parma, who they beat 3-2 on their most recent trip to Stadio Tardini, with Malen inevitably scoring twice.

In fact, Parma have lost 13 of the past 20 league meetings on home turf, so history will not be on their side this weekend.

The hosts have endured a rocky start to the season, already changing coaches, and latest boss Alberto Gilardino only celebrated his first victory shortly before the break.

However, days after stunning Atalanta with a shock 3-0 win in Bergamo, his side were beaten by Bologna in the Derby dell'Emilia.

Parma were reduced to 10 men within eight minutes at the Tardini, after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was dismissed following a VAR review, and they ultimately ended up losing 2-1.

As a result, the Gialloblu sit just one point above the bottom three, with only eight points on the board so far.

The club’s second-highest Serie A scorer during his playing days, Gilardino has a more modest managerial record, and he surely faces another survival scrap after last term’s fruitless fight with Pisa.

Roma have welcomed Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar back during the break, but the latter’s deputy Pierluigi Gollini remains a doubt after missing two games with a back injury.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) are still sidelined, but Gasperini should have everyone else available.

A sure starter up front, Malen sits joint-second in the Capocannoniere rankings with eight Serie A goals, and the Dutch striker also scored for his country in the UEFA Nations League last week.

Meanwhile, Parma will be missing Argentine forward David Romero, who sustained a serious shoulder injury against Bologna.

Diego Carlos is also struggling with a thigh strain, injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe is a massive doubt, and Ndiaye must serve a one-match ban.

In the absence of Romero, teenage starlet Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is another contender.

Parma possible starting lineup:.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Drobnic; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure.

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen.

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.

Latest Update: Top 20 most valuable EFL Championship goalkeepers right now

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The second tier of English football is at the moment home to some of the country's most high-profile clubs, players and upcoming talents who certainly have the potential to go on to bigger and better things.
  • This is the case in various positions, but, unsurprisingly, Championship goalkeepers continue to make plenty of headlines for both good and bad reasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Championship season is now well underway, meaning we have witnessed several inspiring team or individual performances.

The second tier of English football is at the moment home to some of the country's most high-profile clubs, players and upcoming talents who certainly have the potential to go on to bigger and better things.

This is the case in various positions, but, unsurprisingly, Championship goalkeepers continue to make plenty of headlines for both good and bad reasons.

In recent times, we have seen England internationals, Jordan Pickford and James Trafford, excel in the division, and there are many looking to follow in their footsteps.

With that in mind, Football League World have looked at the 20 most-valuable goalkeepers in the second tier right now, owing to Transfermarkt figures.

All figures have been converted from Euro to GBP.

Getting us underway is Preston North End's Daniel Iversen, who is at the moment one of three names valued at £2m.

The Danish shot-stopper rejoined the Deepdale outfit last summer on a free transfer from Leicester City on a four-year contract, but after a mixed first season, this campaign could very much end in relegation for the Lilywhites.

Norwich City parted with £2m to sign Bosnian keeper, Vladan Kovacevic, from Liga Portugal giants, Sporting CP, last summer, and his valuation has since stayed the same.

During that timeframe, the Canaries have endured mixed fortunes on the pitch under Liam Manning and Philippe Clement, while the 28-year-old is yet to make it into a double-figure tally of clean sheets in over 50 appearances.

Jacob Widell Zetterstrom's £1.4m switch to Derby County two summers ago initially looked inspired, but it has been a difficult 2026 for the Swedish international goalkeeper, who is also valued at £2m.

After recovering from an illness earlier this year, the 28-year-old became the subject of interest from Premier League side, Leeds United, but remained at Pride Park, where he has returned to the lineup in a difficult period for John Eustace's side despite a four-game absence with a knee concern.

Alphonse Areola's valuation at West Ham United has taken a major hit following the club's relegation, with the five-time French international's cost now claimed to be in the region of just £2.4m.

This is also impacted by the fact the 33-year-old is out-of-contract at the London Stadium next June, whilst he is yet to make a competitive appearance in 2026/27.

Max O'Leary is also valued at £2.4m right now, but the Irishman has proven to be an inspired signing for West Bromwich Albion.

After being a key figure in the Baggies' survival mission under James Morrison last season, the 30-year-old has already come to his side's rescue on multiple occasions after signing a fresh three-year contract, preventing the most goals in the division whilst having an extremely strong save percentage.

Gregoire Coudert arrived at Burnley from Stade Brestois in July, with the Frenchman the third and final shot-stopper right now with a £2.4m value.

After finding himself on the bench in the Clarets' first eight games under former head coach, Nicky Hayen, Coudert has become a mainstay under Fabio Celestini as the club look to avoid the embarrassment of back-to-back relegations.

Jose Sa has made over 180 appearances for Wolves, having joined from Olympiacos in 2021.

The Portuguese international, despite being in and out of the side last season, is currently Cesar Peixoto's 'number one' at Molineux, although it remains to be seen for how much longer this will be the case.

The 33-year-old is out-of-contract next summer, meaning his current worth is £2.9m.

The only Championship goalkeeper with a £3.3m market value at present is Burnley's Max Weiß.

Weiß moved to Turf Moor last summer from FC Karlsruher in a reported £4.3m deal, but has only made 15 appearances for his current employers so far.

A contributing factor to the German's decrease in value is the fact he is yet to register a clean sheet during that timeframe.

Watford goalkeeper, Federico Ravaglia is up next, with the Hornets seeing the Italian pen a six-year contract at Vicarage Road in the summer.

As such, the 27-year-old is presently valued at £4.1m, having emerged as one of few bright sparks in Hertfordshire during a testing start to the season under Alessio Dionisi.

Arthur Okonkwo impressed during his first season at Championship level with Wrexham last term, but despite keeping 10 clean sheets, was loaned out to divisional rivals, Charlton Athletic, in August.

Despite having a mixed start to life in South London with his temporary employers, and the fact his Red Dragons contract expires next summer, the 25-year-old is also valued at £4.1m right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

It has been revealed that “That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial matter,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

According to recent reports, “We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

Recent findings suggest that “Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”.

Napoli vs Torino - prediction, team news, lineups

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:21.
  • Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.
  • Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:19, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:21.

Separated by one place and one point, Napoli and Torino will return to Serie A duty on Saturday evening, when they meet at Stadio Maradona.

Both sides entered the international break on a grim run of form, sparking talk of another crisis for the hosts.

After setting out with lofty ambitions, Napoli sit 10th in Serie A after 11 matchdays and have lost three of their first four Champions League fixtures.

Struggling both in Europe and Italy's top flight, the Partenopei have won just five times across all competitions since Massimiliano Allegri succeeded Antonio Conte.

That represents their lowest tally of wins at this stage of a campaign since 2003, when they drew 10 of their first 15 games down in Serie B.

Before international football intervened, Allegri's men did earn some credit by holding league leaders Lazio to a 1-1 home draw, having previously suffered damaging defeats to Juventus and Porto.

While they ended their visitors' streak of six consecutive wins - and spurned several second-half chances to seize victory - Napoli ultimately slipped further behind in the top four race.

As a result, the Campanian club cannot afford to drop many more points at the Maradona, where they beat Torino 2-1 in March - their 15th win from the last 22 league meetings.

Torino's only two triumphs during that period both came in Turin, so their last top-flight win in Naples dates all the way back to 2009.

Like their hosts, it has been a mixed start to the season under new management: Ignazio Abate's reign began slowly, but Toro then posted their best run of league wins for six years, before suddenly faltering again.

Having previously taken maximum points from three consecutive games, Toro lost to high-flyers Como and Frosinone, then went into the break with a disappointing home draw against Lecce.

Nonetheless, the Granata have claimed 14 points from their first 11 games for the fifth time in six years, leaving them just one behind Napoli in standings.

So, with a win this weekend, Abate can surpass his former Milan coach Allegri, as ambitious apprentice meets fading master.

Napoli form (all competitions):.

Napoli are still burdened by a significant absence list, but Allegri will have three players back at his disposal on Saturday: David Neres and Costantino Favasuli have recovered from muscular injuries, while Luca Marianucci has served his suspension.

Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Stanislav Lobotka, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo and former Torino skipper Alessandro Buongiorno are still unavailable.

Having starred in Belgium's significant UEFA Nations League victory over Italy, top scorer Kevin De Bruyne will aim to build on his six goal involvements for the Partenopei this season.

While speculation has been stirred up about De Bruyne's future, fan favourite Scott McTominay is set to stay put for now, and he has found the net three times in two games against Torino.

McTominay's international teammate Che Adams is Toro's leading Serie A scorer on four; the Scotland striker could partner Giovanni Simeone, who only scored six times in 83 league appearances for Napoli but has previously scored five goals against them.

Typically lining up just behind the front pair, Nikola Vlasic missed Sunday's clash between Croatia and the Czech Republic due to a minor thigh strain, but he is still expected to play this weekend.

However, Abate has fitness doubts regarding wing-backs Rafik Belghali, Ricardo Rodriguez and Niccolo Fortini.

Napoli possible starting lineup:.

Meret; Beukema, Rrahmani, Marin; Politano, Anguissa, De Bruyne, McTominay, Spinazzola; Vergara; Hojlund.

Torino possible starting lineup:.

Perri; Coco, Ismajli, Comuzzo; Belghali, Fitz-Jim, Mandragora, Cacciamani; Vlasic; Adams, Simeone.

After two defeats and one draw from their last three games, both teams will be desperate for a win.

While Napoli are hampered by injuries and appear disunited, Torino have been leaking too many goals, so more frustration could be on the cards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

According to recent reports, united’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

Industry observers note that “It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick stated. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

Industry observers note that united probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

Sources indicate that carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game initiative.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

Industry observers note that there is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

According to recent reports, mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick remarked. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s newly introduced-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

According to recent reports, carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick remarked. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Industry observers note that dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

Sources indicate that with City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Job done. Now a much bigger test awaits.

Sources indicate that “Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another substantial one on Sunday.”.
