In a recent development, michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

It looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

Industry observers note that “I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

Industry News: Birmingham City backed to revive interest in ex-Burnley star on three conditions

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that birmingham City are flying high in the Championship right now, and as things stand, sit pretty at the top of the Championship table. However, there could still be room for improvement at St Andrews looking ahead to the January window.

Indeed, Birmingham are soaring at the top of the Championship right now, level on points with Middlesbrough and Stoke City but with a superior goal difference.

Head coach Chris Davies has changed the way that the Blues set up and play, becoming a lot more rigid and difficult to beat, reflected in their eight wins, five draws, and just two defeats after 15 league games so far.

It wasn't an especially busy summer in the Second City, with the likes of Jhon Solis, Luis Vazquez, and Dael Fry among those to have joined the club permanently, as there were rumours of a former Championship star heading back to England in the form of Birmingham.

According to TEAMtalk, Birmingham, along with West Ham United and Hull City, were interested in signing Brownhill in the summer, but no deal could be agreed.

Brownhill, 30, has made over 400 appearances in England's top three flights for the likes of Preston North End, Barnsley, Bristol City, and Burnley, netting 18 goals and grabbing six assists from midfield in 42 Championship games for the latter during the 2024/25 campaign.

The Englishman would head to Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Shabab in the summer of 2025 and is nearing a half-century of appearances for the club, but with a contract running until the summer of 2027, could return to England sooner rather than later, as Birmingham could renew their interest in the midfielder this winter.

Football League World's Birmingham fan pundit, Jason Moore, has shared their thoughts on whether they would like to see Brownhill at St Andrews this January if Blues revive their interest in the midfielder.

According to recent reports, jason stated: "You know what? I'm probably going to say no, not because there's no quality there; I'd just be curious about what kind of wage he'd want.

"And to be fair, we've got a pretty settled midfield. Max Bird can't even get a look in at the moment as the six or eight; he's playing at the ten. Paik's not getting a look-in because Solis and Iwata are absolutely solid.

"Don't get me wrong, if the Brownhill deal was there to be done, and it weren't silly wages and something the club wanted to explore, I'd one-hundred per cent back it because, I mean, look at how good he's been in the league.

"So it all depends. The age factor is a big thing for me as well. So it depends on what wages he wants, and if he's hungry to come and battle it out in the Championship again, because, to be fair, out in that part of the world he's probably earning an absolute wedge that Blues, well, let's be honest, no one in the Championship and part of the Premier League can even pay.

"So yeah, it depends if he's hungry, if he wants to come and has to drop a bit in his money, then yeah, bring him in and see if the club backs it.".

In a recent development, do you agree with Jason that Brownhill should only be signed if he is hungry for the move, or should the Blues go all out for his signature regardless? Share your thoughts below!

If Birmingham are indeed in a promotion battle by the time the January window rolls around, you'd be brave to back against the Blues going all out in the window to secure a return to the Premier League.

Brownhill would not cost a hefty fee, though whether he is prepared to take a massive cut in his wages at this stage of his career remains to be seen.

By LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:51 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 15:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar announced his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida said in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46.

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his new side.

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

Sources indicate that he started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

Recent findings suggest that 'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

It has been revealed that 'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'.

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

Bayer Leverkusen will hope to keep pace with the Bundesliga's top four on Saturday, when they take on visitors SC Paderborn at BayArena.

The hosts come into the clash with 16 points after nine matchweeks and could end the weekend five points from the top four, whereas 13th-placed Paderborn have 10 points.

Leverkusen are two points from fourth-placed RB Leipzig and three points from third-placed Freiburg, but only four points separate them from 11th-placed Hamburger SV.

Manager Carles Martinez oversaw a 2-1 victory against FC Koln on November 8 prior to the international break, and that brought to an end a losing streak of two games.

The hosts have also lost two of their last three Bundesliga fixtures, conceding eight goals while scoring on four occasions.

Leverkusen's two most recent home clashes saw them lose 1-0 against Marseille in the Europa League on November 5 and 4-2 against Stuttgart in the German top flight on October 31.

However, it should be noted that they triumphed in each of their first five clashes at BayArena this season, netting at least two goals in each contest.

Paderborn were held to a 2-2 stalemate by Eintracht Frankfurt on November 7 before the international break, and that extended their undefeated streak in the league to four outings.

The club only won once in that time, while they managed to score five goals and keep two clean sheets, with all four of the goals they conceded coming in two separate 2-2 draws.

Head coach Ralf Kettemann will hope to earn a first away victory in five matches, though a draw would be the club's fourth in that period.

The visitors have failed to find the back of the net in three of their four Bundesliga matches on the road this campaign, though they also prevented opponents from scoring twice.

A win for Paderborn would be their first ever success against Leverkusen, with the hosts having beaten the visitors in six of their seven meetings.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 17:22.

After both swapping their typical midtable mediocrity for an exciting promotion race, Stoke City and Birmingham City clash at the bet365 Stadium for a Championship match on Saturday afternoon.

The Potters enjoyed a dramatic success at Portsmouth prior to the November international break, whilst Blues picked up a last-minute victory over Swansea City in the Second City.

In the build-up to this weekend, Stoke head coach Mark Robins has revealed that a top-eight finish was the target set in August, however, it appears that his Staffordshire outfit could be capable of much more.

After losing their first three matches, the Potters have been defeated in just one of their past 12 second-tier contests - a run which includes four wins and a single draw in their past five clashes.

Before the final international break of the calendar year, Stoke made it three straight victories with a 2-1 triumph at Fratton Park, where second-half goals from Jack McGlynn and Ben Wilmot secured maximum points.

With their sole defeat since August coming against promotion favourites Middlesbrough, Robins's men have flown up to third position in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham.

For all of the positivity around the Potters, they have not been untouchable at the bet365 Stadium in recent times, managing just a single win over bottom side Preston North End across their past three home contests.

After a humiliating 6-1 defeat by Brentford in the EFL Cup on August 25, many Birmingham City supporters were calling for the head of manager Chris Davies, who has since masterminded a remarkable turnaround in the Second City.

Between the past two international breaks, Blues have established themselves as the team to beat in the Championship, winning six of their past seven league fixtures, including four straight home successes.

Following comfortable St Andrew's @ Knighthead Park wins over Preston (4-0), Queens Park Rangers (3-0) and Millwall (3-0), Birmingham needed a last-gasp Jay Stansfield goal to conquer Swansea on November 7.

Scoring on three occasions in the past two matches, £20m man Stansfield stepped up to the goalscoring plate in the absence of August Priske, with Max Bird entering the starting XI and also performing excellently.

Rather remarkably, Blues are sitting on the summit of the Championship table for the first time since the 2008-09 season - the campaign in which they last secured promotion to the Premier League under Alex McLeish.

Stoke have a number of injury doubts ahead of this weekend's top-of-the-table clash, including youngster Lamine Cisse and defender Eric Bocat.

Providing plenty of experience to the Potters ranks, Aaron Cresswell has not featured since May in a competitive game due to a knee problem.

Scoring for Slovakia in the Nations League on Monday, striker Robert Bozenik arrives back in Staffordshire full of confidence.

Birmingham boast international stars of their own, with Colombia's Jhon Solis and Canada's Liam Millar returning from duty unscathed.

Sitting out of selection for their nations over the past fortnight, goalkeeper James Beadle and Priske are both available for this weekend.

As a result, second-choice stopper Ryan Allsop will likely return to the bench and Bird could drop out of the XI despite impressive displays recently.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The whole of English football was devastated to learn that Tony Mowbray will once again have to step away from management.

The 62-year-old is facing a fresh set of health complications that requires his immediate attention, which means he has had to walk away from his job at Rovers for the time being.

Confirmed via Blackburn Rovers’ official club website, Mowbray praised the players, coaching staff, supporters and ownership group for their support and work ever since stepping back into the role, while asking for privacy as he enters his latest battle.

Mowbray, in a statement, noted: “Unfortunately, due to health challenges, I have to step back from my role as Head Coach of Blackburn Rovers.

Sources indicate that “I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

It has been revealed that “Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

“To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

“I’m grateful to the Owners and Suhail for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

“I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time.

“Thank you for your understanding.

One of the most loved managers in the English game, it’s deeply saddening that Mowbray has once again had to step away due to his health, and it’s particularly difficult for Blackburn supporters to stomach given they had a realistic chance of a play-off push under his leadership.

While Mowbray works his way back to full fitness, Blackburn will need some form of interim manager to come in and steady the ship, and there could be a perfect candidate, who would surely be welcomed back with open arms given the work he did at Ewood Park last season.

While the tone of Tony Mowbray’s message appeared as if he wasn’t coming back to manage Blackburn Rovers again, the 62-year-old is reportedly only stepping away from his role, with the possibility of a return once he is fully recovered.

A tweet by journalist Elliott Jackson revealed that Mowbray hasn’t resigned or fully stepped down, but instead will be away for a period to fully focus on his health, although there is no timeframe on how long he will be away from his post for.

The club are believed to not be looking for a successor right now, meaning that an interim manager to step in over the short-term is likelier before Mowbray can make a return.

Blackburn did confirm Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will take responsibility for first-team duties for the time being, but with Mowbray expected to be out for a significant period of time, you do feel a more experienced head is needed over the long-term so Rovers are not at risk of sliding down the standings.

Therefore, making a move to bring someone like Michael O’Neill back to the club could be an inspired move.

O’Neill won the hearts of the Blackburn faithful when stepping into the job back in February, succeeding Valerien Ismael and juggling that role with his usual commitments to the Northern Ireland national side.

22nd in the Championship with 15 games to play, O’Neill won five, drew five and lost five of those remaining matches, turning the tide as Blackburn finished 20th in the second tier and avoided relegation, although there was disappointment in May when O’Neill confirmed he wouldn’t be taking the job permanently, stating he would be unable to do both roles and would have to choose one or the other.

Meanwhile, O’Neill has continued to prove his managerial credentials on the international front with Northern Ireland, helping them top their UEFA Nations League B Group, overcoming the likes of Hungary, Ukraine and Georgia.

Not to mention that they only conceded one goal throughout the league phase too, with that incidentally coming in their final game against Hungary where they battled to a 1-1 draw.

Esteemed journalist Henry Winter labelled O’Neill’s work at Northern Ireland in the Nations League as “one of the finest managerial achievements so far this season”, with his level of impact on the national stage going far from unnoticed.

Now Tony Mowbray has temporarily departed, it’s vitally important that Blackburn Rovers get another manager in on an interim basis to steady the ship and help keep the club fighting towards the upper end of the table.

And once again, that could suit Michael O’Neill down to the ground, who wouldn’t have any long-term ties but could once again take over the mantle for however long he is needed.

What puts Blackburn in a strong position to attract O’Neill to return to the club is the fact that there is now no more international football until March 2027, meaning that it would be favourable for the Northern Ireland manager to step back into club football and reunite with a club where he is so loved from his previous work.

Blackburn Rovers fans, would you bring Michael O'Neill back to Ewood Park on an interim basis? Could he be the man to keep your promotion hopes intact? Leave your thoughts in the comments!

With Blackburn needing a strong and experienced manager to keep their season on an upward trajectory and O’Neill wanting or needing to keep busy over such a long pause from the international game, it seems a partnership that would really benefit both parties, and given the success O’Neill has achieved in his managerial career in recent times, you would expect Blackburn to fly high under his leadership once again and really push to be in contention for promotion come the end of the season.

It’s certainly a deal most of the Blackburn faithful would want to see happen, so if the club are serious about their promotion ambitions, then linking back up with O’Neill on a similar deal to the one he was on last campaign is something they have to explore and get sorted as promptly as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

No matter how history judges his time in charge of Scotland, no one will ever accuse Sebastien Pocognoli of leaving a single stone unturned.

Intense, intelligent and highly demanding, the Belgian has already shown himself to be substantial on the small things which can combine to make a significant difference.

Che Adams discovered this for himself in September, even though an injury prevented him from being part of the newly introduced man’s first get together in La Manga.

‘I heard from the manager the last time when I wasn’t in the camp,’ he revealed.

In a recent development, ‘He loves a FaceTime call. I think he’s taken a few of the boys by surprise when they’ve been out walking their dogs and stuff. I think KT (Kieran Tierney) was out for a walk when he phoned him.

Industry observers note that ‘He just calls out of the blue and has done it to a few of the boys. It’s unexpected and it’s different because we’ve never experienced something like that. But it’s good.

Che Adams' appearance against North Macedonia was his first under Sebastien Pocognoli.

Striker Adams states Pocognoli is more intense than his predecessor and is 'with the times'.

John McGinn is within six goals of the scoring record shared by Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

‘In the last camp when I was out injured, he was on asking how my injury was, how long I’d be out for and if I still wanted to be part of it.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The camps haven’t changed much, but the manager is definitely more intense. I think it’s the European style of play and thinking. It’s going to take time for him to understand the boys, understand us as players and understand us as a squad.

‘But he’s really bought into it and wants to help us do well.’.

Industry observers note that hang on a minute. A manager who’s more intense than Steve Clarke? You could be forgiven for thinking that’s simply not possible. But Adams feels it is very much the case.

‘With Steve you could have a laugh and you can do that with this gaffer as well,’ he explained.

‘But he’s a lot more intense in terms of detail off the pitch telling you where to be and what to do.

‘This gaffer has good ideas, a good approach to the game.

‘He is with the times, really. Everyone’s buying into it and I definitely think we’ll see the benefits.’.

John McGinn believes it could be as long as 18 months before it all comes up roses. But, in football, you rarely get that long.

Starting in St Gallen tomorrow, the Belgian could do with some green shoots emerging.

‘He’s a few years younger (than Clarke) and has a different philosophy on how he wants his team to play,’ added Adams.

‘It just takes time to click, but it’s up to us as players now to show we can do what he wants.

‘We have been together for a number of years now, so we know each other’s games.

‘You could see on Friday us starting to put the manager’s things in practice. We won a lot of balls high with our pressing.

‘He noted to us after the game that it’s about the killer moments and we probably didn’t capitalise on them enough. But it was a win and the first one for the gaffer at Hampden.

‘For every manager they need time, but you saw spells there where the movements and patterns of play were very good.

‘It was very important to get the win and build up the confidence.

‘You’ve also got to keep in context things like that it was Luke Graham’s first start for us, but he had the confidence to play those passes in the build-up.

‘So, you have to credit the manager for putting the belief in the young players who have come in as well.’.

The comfort for Pocognoli throughout a time of transition is that he can still depend on the old stagers who were central to the success under his predecessor.

On the night when Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps, McGinn claimed a double to put himself within six goals of the scoring record jointly held by Dalglish and Denis Law.

Having just turned 32, there is every chance that the Aston Villa captain can soon claim his own slice of history.

‘It’s amazing for John, he’s such a great person and he deserves it,’ noted Adams.

‘Everyone can see what he’s done for club and country, he puts his heart on his sleeve and gives everything.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with him. I really hope he does do it - and I think he will.

‘He’s not going to stop until he does.

In a recent development, ‘Everyone is so pleased for him, he’s the best person I’ve met in football. When I came into the squad I didn’t think we’d have people who would achieve these kind of things.

Industry observers note that ‘I have loved every single minute of it. We have done some great things here.

It has been revealed that ‘We have been to three major tournaments now, people are making personal achievements as well. But as a team and as a squad it’s about taking that next step now in tournaments.

Sources indicate that ‘It’s a pleasure to play with these boys. They’re legends of football.’.

Tech Report: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4646 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

It has been revealed that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso noted: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

In a recent development, “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

In a recent development, this is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

Recent findings suggest that none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also highlighted quality and a threat. The joke is at the moment on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

In a recent development, “Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

Recent findings suggest that “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he stated. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

It has been revealed that chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

Sources indicate that it was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

It has been revealed that we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

In a recent development, we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Recent findings suggest that eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

It has been revealed that fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

It has been revealed that and as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

Sources indicate that you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Recent findings suggest that hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

It has been revealed that that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Recent findings suggest that bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

According to recent reports, matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Industry observers note that tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a fresh left-back in due course.

In a recent development, so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

Industry observers note that austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. According to recent reports, wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:24, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:27.

Having left for the international break on a rare low, Como will aim to resume their stellar start to the season when Cagliari visit Stadio Sinigaglia on Saturday.

Not only are the Lariani making a massive impact in Europe, they have been breaking new ground in Serie A - but defeat to the champions recently slowed their charge towards the top four.

Como have caught the eye in this season's Champions League - notably following their famous 4-1 defeat of Manchester United with a ruthless 9-1 destruction of Lens - and they also have big ambitions in Serie A.

Remarkably, the European rookies sit above Barcelona and Bayern Munich in UEFA's top competition, and they had posted six straight wins across all competitions before facing Inter Milan last time out.

Overseen by one of football's most-wanted coaches, the Lariani scored 22 goals and conceded just four during that hot streak, but it came to an abrupt end at San Siro.

Como's 12th consecutive league defeat to Inter left Cesc Fabregas and co five points behind the Scudetto holders, while costing them their place in the top four.

As a manager, Fabregas has yet to conquer Inter in either Serie A or the Coppa Italia, but his team tend to take care of business against Italy's lesser lights.

Now heading back to base, Como have kept clean sheets in their last three league matches at the Sinigaglia, where they have never lost a top-flight clash against Cagliari.

Beaten 2-1 when the pair most recently met, Cagliari's last Serie A win over Como dates back to March 1982 - albeit both clubs have spent plenty of time outside the top tier.

This term, the Sardinian side will head to Lombardy full of confidence, as they sit just inside the top half following a largely positive start to the current campaign.

Hurtling out of the blocks, Fabio Pisacane's men claimed four victories from their opening five fixtures - only losing to Inter - before slipping back into the pack with a less successful run.

Yet, when facing down Frosinone after suffering four consecutive defeats, Cagliari came out on top: Michel Adopo's goal gave them a 1-0 win over the newly promoted high-flyers.

All told, a haul of 16 points from their first 11 matches represents the Rossoblu's best top-flight start since 2019, and Pisacane has been handed much of the credit.

Continuing an injury-hit start to his Como career, Moise Kean has suffered a setback in his recovery from a tibia problem and could be sidelined for several more weeks.

Wide men Jayden Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are also unavailable, but Fabregas hopes to have Assane Diao and Trevoh Chalobah back in the squad.

The hosts' star man, Nico Paz helped Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 earlier this week, scoring his first international brace.

Recent findings suggest that the 22-year-old has already posted 14 goal involvements for Como this season, attracting interest from Europe's top clubs. Curiously, though, just two of his last 11 Serie A strikes have come on home soil.

While Paz should link up with Greece striker Tasos Douvikas in the final third, Cagliari's front line may be led by Paul Mendy and Daniel Maldini - the latter of whom has found the net five times this term.

Although Pisacane can recall Adam Obert after the left-back served a suspension against Frosinone, several men are still missing through injury.

Alieu Fadera and Mattia Felici have been ruled out, while M'Bala Nzola (flexor), Harry Winks (back) and Yerry Mina (thigh) are all struggling to return in time.

Butez; Couto, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Milla; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas.

Cagliari possible starting lineup:.

Caprile; Ze Pedro, Kofler, Rodriguez, Obert; Adopo, Romano, Deiola; Fazzini, Maldini; Mendy.

Free-flowing Como can score from all quarters, while Cagliari must head to the mainland on a run of three away defeats, in which they shipped 10 goals.

So, the hosts will resume winning ways after their setback in Milan, keeping them on the tails of Italy's top three.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City's start to the Championship season under Mark Robins has caught plenty of attention, with the Potters, for once, making headlines for the right reasons.

It has been well-documented that the Potters are yet to finish inside the second tier's top-half following relegation from the Premier League in 2018.

This time last season, Robins' side found themselves in a similar position to their current standing of third, as only goal difference separates them from league leaders, Birmingham City.

However, there is a strong feeling that City could last the course of the 46-game season in the promotion mix if their key men continue living up to the bill.

Stoke have parted with plenty of cash since their top-flight relegation, and much of it has gone to waste given their league finishes.

Eight-figure fees for the likes of Benik Afobe and Tom Ince are enough to make supporters cringe, with neither making the desired impact, but this summer, they were joined by Ethan Galbraith on this particular front, with it taking £10m to prize the Northern Ireland international away from divisional rivals, Swansea City.

Galbraith, 25, previously excelled in both central midfield and right-back roles for Leyton Orient in League One, and took such form with him to South Wales under Alan Sheehan and Vitor Matos.

With the Swans only parting with £1.5m to secure his services, it is a testament to how promptly Galbraith adapted to the Championship's rigours as an all-action midfielder, with his former employers making at least £8.5m worth of profit, but Stoke have certainly been the early winners of said deal.

Given Swansea finished six places and nine points clear of Stoke in 2025/26, plenty of eyebrows were raised over Galbraith's ambition when opting to return north.

Despite only registering five goal contributions last term for the Welsh side, Galbraith still earned plenty of praise from Championship onlookers, as well as former Stoke and current Northern Ireland boss, Michael O'Neill.

They were also joined by television personality and talkSPORT host, Jeff Stelling, who pinpointed the deal as the standout acquisition of the summer, even ahead of West Ham United's EFL record buy for Celtic's Arne Engels.

"Best signing for me, and this will please Stoke fans, not much to shout about in recent seasons, they signed Ethan Galbraith, paid around £10million for him from Swansea," noted Stellling.

"I've always been impressed with him; I saw him for Swansea and Northern Ireland as well, a former Manchester United kid, he's 25 now.

"I thought he had a sniff of a move to the Premier League, to be honest, so for Stoke, I think that's a real coup.".

Galbraith's career path means there has been plenty of interest in his performances from a young age, having come through the Red Devils academy between 2017 and 2019, before making a solitary first-team appearance against Astana in the UEFA Europa League.

The following pre-season, Galbraith found himself in Ole Gunnar Solksjaer's first-team plans, with it previously being claimed by a club insider: "He's the best young player outside the core first-team group at the club.".

During an encounter with Aston Villa, Solksjaer publicly revealed that Galbraith needed to aclimatise to the pace of play against top-level performers compared to at youth level, and Stoke are currently the beneficiaries of such a vast improvement.

Galbraith may have been one of several eye-catching transfer moves made by Stoke this summer, especially due to the fee in question, but it is one which could land the club in excess of £200m in the coming months.

No Potters player has registered more goal contributions than the 21-time international's seven, which outperforms his expected combined number of just 3.2, further highlighting his talismanic influence.

Galbraith has also created 25 chances for his teammates, whilst also averaging 8.1 line-breaking passes and 5 recovery tackles per 90 minutes.

It has been revealed that stoke fans, is Ethan Galbraith the signing of the season in the Championship? Comment below!

Given his versatile nature, if he remains injury-free and staves off further suspensions, having missed the recent away success at Blackburn Rovers following a fifth yellow card, Robins and Stoke will be laughing, with Galbraith's valuation likely to continue increasing in the near future, such is his importance.

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:35, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 18:36.

Thomas Frank has provided his first injury enhancement as Crystal Palace manager ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Coventry City at the CBS Arena.

Nine months after his sacking by Tottenham Hotspur, Frank was appointed the new Eagles boss on Monday, just five days after Pierre Sage was relieved of his duties.

The Dane has taken over a Palace side that sits rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 top-flight fixtures, including a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool before the international break.

Defender Takehiro Tomiyasu has been sidelined for the last nine matches in all competitions with a calf injury, while last season’s top scorer Ismaila Sarr has been limited to only 15 minutes of Premier League action this term due to an ongoing groin problem.

Speaking at a press conference on Thursday afternoon, Frank confirmed that both players will not be ready to return for the trip to Coventry.

"I can say that Tomiyasu will be back training next week," Frank told reporters. "On Sarr, it'll be touch and go when he can start training. It's a groin injury so you need to be careful.

Industry observers note that "You need to be aware with those injuries about how much you push. That could take a little longer time. You need to make sure that you don't take two steps forward, to then take two steps back.

It has been revealed that "This could take a little longer. He'll not necessarily be on the pitch next week.".

Chadi Riad (knee) remains a long-term injury absentee for Palace, while there was no mention of Jorgen Strand Larsen at Frank’s press conference, but the striker has been spotted in training this week after withdrawing from the Norway squad with an ankle problem.

Meanwhile, striker Jean-Philippe Mateta will serve the second of a three-match suspension this weekend following his red card against Tottenham at the end of last month.

Palace are hoping for an immediate manager bounce under Frank following a disappointing run of four straight defeats in the Premier League.

The Eagles won their first four visits to the CBS Arena between 2005 and 2008, but are winless in their last four across all tournaments between 2009 and their most recent trip in 2012 (D2 L2).

Discussing the challenge of facing Coventry in his first game as Palace boss, Frank stated: "I know it'll be difficult.

"But I also trust the boys, I know we'll perform on Saturday. We just need a little margin to go in our favour.".

Victory for Palace could see them climb off the foot of the table and out of the relegation zone up to as high as 16th place – above Coventry presently in 17th – if other results go their way this weekend.

There is no real debate that, given their recent trajectory, Aston Villa run the rule in the West Midlands in terms of on-pitch matters, with Birmingham City and West Bromwich Albion hoping to get close to such levels in the near future.

The Villans ended a 30-year wait for major silverware in May by winning the UEFA Europa League final against SC Freiburg, having also finished fourth in the Premier League for the second time in three seasons.

As such, Unai Emery's side are competing in the UEFA Champions League yet again, which has provided at least eight midweek clashes for the B6 club between September and January - four of which are at Villa Park.

Midweek encounters are nothing new to Blues and Albion though, such is the gruelling nature of the Championship's 46-game schedule, which both Chris Davies and James Morrison are hoping to successfully navigate.

There is, at the moment, every chance at least one local derby could be on the agenda in next season's top-flight, with local authorities perhaps getting served an unwanted reminder of the chaos attached to such fixtures next month.

It is so often the case that European and domestic schedules involving English sides coincide throughout the season, but December 8th will firmly see the spotlight cast on the West Midlands for this particular reason.

The Championship calendar was released two months before the Champions League 'league phase' draw took place in Monaco, with Birmingham hosting Watford at St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park in an 8PM kick-off, whilst West Brom welcome Cardiff City to The Hawthorns that same evening at 7:45PM.

It is nothing latest to see Blues and Albion's midweek home fixtures on the same date, with around five miles separating the two stadiums, and this was indeed the case earlier this month when Millwall were dispatched 4-0 in B9, whilst the Baggies drew with Southampton.

However, adding the visit of Champions League winners, Paris Saint-Germain, to Villa Park, which is equidistant between the two Championship stadiums, creates a whole new dilemma for West Midlands police, especially after reports of trouble between French fans and those from Birmingham in April 2025 on the continent before the first of two quarter-final clashes.

All three local rivals, of course, attract supporters beyond the city of Birmingham and the neighbouring town of West Bromwich, although when factoring in those in the away ends into the equation, local transport staff could be set for a busy evening.

According to recent reports, the Hawthorns is situated on a West Midlands Metro and local train line out of Birmingham Snow Hill, allowing plenty of access for those arriving beyond B71. There are multiple ways of making your way to Villa Park and St. Andrew's too, but that doesn't decrease the chances of rival fans potentially clashing with each other.

National Express West Midlands run shuttle buses labelled '1982' and '1875' to both stadiums, with both starting journeys in the vicinity of Birmingham New Street station, whilst those journeying to B6 can also take train journeys to Aston and Witton stations.

Will you be attending one of these three fixtures? Comment below!

No official comment is yet to be made by local authorities, which is only adding to such discourse.

For those who support Villa and Birmingham, it is still particularly unusual for the Second City rivals to be the home sides on the same evening, even though it happened on two occasions during the 2024/25 campaign.

After returning to European football's elite competition for the first time in 43 years, Emery's side welcomed Bayern Munich and Bologna to Villa Park on the 2nd and 22nd October 2024, winning famously against the German giants through Jhon Duran's lob, before seeing off the Italians 2-0 three weeks later.

On those same nights, Blues hosted Huddersfield Town and Bolton Wanderers, with Davies' side emerging 1-0 and 2-0 victors in their own midweek encounters.

In terms of on-pitch matters, similar feats will be welcomed by the rival fanbases, whilst those in the police force will be praying for no disorder on the streets.

Published: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 15 November 2026.

Sebastien Pocognoli has conceded that he doesn’t have 18 months to demonstrate that Scotland are on the right track under him.

Appointed Steve Clarke’s successor in the summer, the Belgian’s attempts to bring in fresh faces and a fresh style of play has produced mixed results in his opening five Nations League games.

Following Friday’s win over North Macedonia, John McGinn warned the Tartan Army that it could take as long as 18 months for everything to click into place.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Asked if he felt he had to deliver sooner, he stated: ‘Yeah, for sure, but we’re only talking about 18 months because John said that. He could have said 15 months. I don’t know. But, for sure, it needs to be quicker.

According to recent reports, ‘In 18 months, it will be the time of the Euros and that is what he meant. We have to go there and be prepared for this in 18 months’ time.

Sebastien Pocognoli  notes his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘For sure, game after game, we need to see improvement.

‘Some new faces will come back in March. So, step by step we will have more ideas and in one month’s time a lot can change also.’.

McGinn also remarked that the players were fully behind the manager, reiterating the point previously made by Andy Robertson and Scott McTominay.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most notable part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager mentioned: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

Pocognoli’s side were booed off at half-time on Friday with criticism of the performance persisting despite them going on to win the game.

In a recent development, but the manager claims he’s oblivious to wider concerns about the performances to date, saying: ‘No, I’m not aware of this. That’s why I was surprised (at the question).

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

Industry observers note that ‘Yes, there were some boos at half-time. I think that’s part of it, it’s been like this for years.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

Sources indicate that ‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

‘But there there were also a lot of positives after the North Macedonia game.

‘I was the first one to say calm down as we need to see more.’.

Thomas Frank makes exciting Crystal Palace promise after trading Australia break for Premier League return

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.
  • Newly introduced Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.
  • The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s new boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 18:49.

Newly introduced Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank has vowed to give his “very best” to ensure that the Eagles will avoid relegation from the Premier League this season.

The 53-year-old was officially unveiled as Palace’s new boss on Monday, just five days after the sacking of his predecessor Pierre Sage who lasted less than five months at Selhurst Park.

Frank has taken over an Eagles outfit that is sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of their opening 10 games and conceding a division-high 24 goals.

The Dane was believed to be on Palace’s radar in the summer, but he made it clear that he wanted an extended break away from management before assessing his options.

Frank now feels that the time is right to return to the Premier League “circus” for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February after a underwhelming eight-month spell in charge, winning just 34.2% of his 38 games in North London.

Remembered fondly for his successful seven-year tenure as Brentford boss, Frank is excited to take the reins at an “iconic” club in the form of Crystal Palace and is confident that he can steer them away from trouble.

Speaking at his first press conference on Thursday afternoon ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash at Coventry City, Frank told reporters: "It's good to be back! It's a little bit of surprise, the feeling I have in the body; how good it feels.

"Of course I stated yes for a reason, to join Palace and go back into the circus and into the Premier League.

"It's just so good to be back and I'm in no doubt there won't be times where it won't feel like that, but I'm happy to be here.".

"For me Palace is an iconic club in England and it's also shown that, in many years in the Premier League, doing fantastic things,” Frank added.

"Selhurst Park is a fantastic place to go, to watch football, to feel the atmosphere, to feel a proper game.

It has been revealed that "I think Palace, when I've faced them over the years have always been a tough team to play. It's always been difficult.".

Frank was enjoying a break away from football in Australia with his family, but he was persuaded by Crystal Palace to return to the Premier League in the middle of a season.

"It's been of course extremely busy. In every aspect, of course, to join a pre-season is a privilege and I've had the privilege to do that in the other clubs I've been in,” remarked the Dane.

"The good thing is that you want to implement all your ideas, and that will take some time to hit the ground running, but I know what I want and the direction we should go in.

"Timing - in life and football - is everything. I was enjoying my life in Australia. It's pretty nice down there. Nice weather together with the family. And I'm a person that really enjoys football, it is my life. It's scary to feel how I feel, how it feels to be back.

"I'll speak to my good friend Roy [Hodgson] of course and speak to him - I don't want to go as long as he did - but it's good, that feeling. Good to be back.".

Commenting on improving results at Selhurst Park and moving away from the relegation zone, Frank added: "I'm looking forward to come in to do everything I can to help the team, the club.

"I think it's a very talented squad. I think it's got good potential in every aspect.

"Of course we are in a position where we don't want to be, and I'll do my very best together with the staff and players to make sure we're in a much better position when the season is done.".

Crystal Palace, who have spent the last 14 years in the top flight, could climb out of the relegation zone if they end their four-match losing streak with a victory at Coventry this weekend and other results go their way.

Meanwhile, Frank has also provided a fresh injury update on attacker Ismaila Sarr and defender Takehiro Tomiyasu ahead of their trip to the CBS Arena.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swansea City have confirmed that Strasbourg have appointed Vitor Matos as their newly introduced head coach, and the move couldn't have come at a worse time, with three tough games in the next week, culminating in the South Wales derby against Cardiff City.
  • Matos oversaw an early run to the Championship summit at the Swansea.com Stadium, playing a high-intensity, pressing style of football out of possession, while also being one of the best teams with the ball in the second tier.
  • Recent findings suggest that even with four defeats in their last five games leading up to the November international break, the Swans were still three points off top spot, sitting in sixth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City have confirmed that Strasbourg have appointed Vitor Matos as their newly introduced head coach, and the move couldn't have come at a worse time, with three tough games in the next week, culminating in the South Wales derby against Cardiff City.

Matos oversaw an early run to the Championship summit at the Swansea.com Stadium, playing a high-intensity, pressing style of football out of possession, while also being one of the best teams with the ball in the second tier.

Recent findings suggest that even with four defeats in their last five games leading up to the November international break, the Swans were still three points off top spot, sitting in sixth. For a side who hadn't been near a play-off spot for five seasons before this one, the ceiling under Matos was, understandably, exciting.

Therefore, the departure to a struggling Ligue 1 side and the haste with which it occurred throughout this week have stung, and Swansea need to pick themselves up immediately, with games against West Brom and Middlesbrough, two fellow promotion hopefuls, and Cardiff in the South Wales derby in the first week back.

In the interim, Swansea have revealed that club legends Ashley Williams, Leon Brittain, Joe Allen and Kris O'Leary, who boast a combined 1,400 appearances for the club during their respective playing days, will be in charge of Saturday's clash with West Brom.

Whether they'll still be in the dugout by the end of next week and for the visit of Cardiff is still to be seen. FLW's Bluebirds fan pundit, Matt Hall, is torn about whether this would give his side a bit of an advantage in their first derby in over a year,.

"First and foremost, as a Cardiff fan, it's quite enjoyable to see this happen to your rival club, but I'm not 100% sure how huge a boost this is in terms of their form in general; they do have some hard games before the South Wales Derby," he noted.

According to recent reports, "I think it's stating the obvious that if those four guys are in charge in three games' time, that, tactically, they won't stand a chance against BBM [Brian Barry-Murphy]. He is on another stratosphere compared to most managers, let alone ones who haven't managed before.".

Hall does admit that having four ex-Swans players in charge of the derby could give them an emotional edge, though, as they'll know exactly how to get their squad up for one of the biggest games in their calendar.

The fan pundit initially thought that they'd have the advantage in that regard, given how many academy graduates and Welshmen are presently in their squad.

"Obviously, the counter-argument I'd have to the South Wales Derby is that one of my confidences going into the derbies was that they'd sold a lot of their homegrown players; it is just Ben Cabango left," he explained.

"Whereas we've got an entire squad basically full of academy players, so it's almost a reverse of what it's been over the past few years, when it's always been the case where they've gone into the game with two to three academy players in the lineup who just get it, and they can translate that across the squad.

"Going into that game, though, those coaches will absolutely get them up for the game. There's every possibility, with our away form, that they will just turn that game into a pure passionate scrap and that can even it out.".

It has been revealed that do you think Cardiff City have been handed an advantage after Vitor Matos left Swansea City? Let us know in the comments.

There's also the potential that, with two tough games on the Saturday and Tuesday before the derby, paired with the departure of a clearly influential head coach in Matos, Swansea could go into the match against Cardiff off the back of six losses in seven, given they've lost four of their last five.

Confidence could be low, and Brian Barry-Murphy's side could take advantage, even if a quartet of ex-Swans are trying to stoke some emotion.

"I don't expect them to get much from West Brom or Middlesbrough before the derby, so the confidence could be on the floor; they've lost four of the last five already, it could go either way.".

Barry-Murphy doesn't fall into the young side of the 'young, up-and-coming managers' in the EFL, but he's definitely one of the more fascinating coaches with one of the highest ceilings.

With Matos departing, it begs the question: which other Championship coaches could follow suit and make the step-up to a top-flight club at some point this season?

According to recent reports, hall doesn't think that the Irishman would make that step, though. Wherever he's gone, whether that be Rochdale or Manchester City's development squad, he's stayed his course, and he's confident that the project at Cardiff still suits him.

Industry observers note that "In terms of whether I'm concerned that the same could happen to BBM, absolutely not," he said. "I think you have to look at the character of the manager as well.

It has been revealed that "Vitor Matos left Maritimo after 12 games, which showed the sort of character he is. You look at BBM; he only left for Man City when he was sacked by Rochdale. He then stayed his course at City until he felt it was time to move on.

"He's been very patient to make sure he gets the right job, and he's shown nothing but gratitude to Cardiff for the opportunity that he's been given.".

The fan pundit does admit that there's every possibility that he could move on if he doesn't think that he can take Cardiff any further. But with the higher-ups allowing him to bed in young players from the academy and play his style of football at this level, he feels that he's still enjoying his time in the Welsh capital.

Industry observers note that "He's a man of high morals, but that will only go so far. I think if we stop allowing him to progress the club, then I think there will be a time when he may move on, but while we are giving him what he wants and the club is on an upward trajectory, I don't see why he would move.

"Especially as what he does is so built around having an academy, and in the pyramid there are not many clubs, if any, who have a better set-up than us right now, at least in terms of the amount of players in our first team.

"It's interesting; I've never felt too worried about him being poached, if I'm honest.".

The South Wales derby was always going to be a fascinating watch this season. Despite being at opposing ends of the table, not much actually separates either side per the underlying numbers. Opta's expected table has them eighth and ninth.

They're both heavy possession teams, but it would have been interesting to see how Cardiff approached the game away from home against a side that won't allow them to build up as patiently as others this season.

That's now possibly changed, though, with the departure of Matos, but if anything, it's added an extra layer to what is already a game filled with storylines.

You don't need to sell the South Wales Derby; it's one of the fiercest games in the EFL, and with them not in the same division last season, absence will definitely not have made the heart grow fonder; quite the opposite, actually.

So, with the potential for it to be a quartet of ex-players in the Swansea dugout, or perhaps the first game for a newly introduced head coach, it's definitely going to be one to keep an eye on next Sunday.

  • Industry observers note that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.

Industry observers note that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he noted. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

In a recent development, spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

Sources indicate that “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This fresh stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.
