Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

Sources indicate that this game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

  • Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.
  • A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:31.

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw across seven games in all competitions, Aston Villa have failed to come out on top in any of their last four matches (D2 L2), with their latest setback sparking a furious reaction from manager Unai Emery.

Villa allowed Man United to come from two goals behind twice and salvage a point in a chaotic 4-4 draw at Old Trafford prior to the international break, with the visitors conceding two goals in stoppage time to be denied what would have been just their third win at the Theatre of Dreams in 32 visits.

Three wins, four draws and three defeats have been posted by the Midlands club in 10 top-flight games this term, leaving them sitting 10th in the Premier League table and five points behind the top four where they finished last season.

Since the beginning of October, Villa have dropped a joint-division-high six points from winning positions, while their defensive concerns remain having conceded in 13 of their 16 matches across all competitions this season.

Heading into Emery’s 150th Premier League game in charge this weekend, Villa have found the net 14 times across a five-game unbeaten home run (W3 D2), while they have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight meetings with Sunderland (W5 D6) – a 3-1 away defeat in January 2016.

Sunderland ended a miserable seven-game winless run in the Premier League with a much-needed 1-0 triumph over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light before the international break, courtesy of a first-half penalty from Enzo Le Fee.

Head coach Regis Le Bris was delighted to see his Black Cats side ‘re-connect with our identity and our fans’ after delivering a gritty and disciplined display that helped them climb off the foot of the Premier League table for the first time in three weeks.

Now sitting 19th and only three points behind Hull in 13th spot, Sunderland will be looking to win consecutive top-flight games for the first time this season when they make the trip to Villa Park this weekend, as well as end their five-game winless streak on the road.

The Black Cats sit rock bottom of the away form table having accumulated only one point (D1 L4) and conceded a joint-division-high 13 goals, including three in a 3-1 defeat at Coventry City at the end of last month.

Sunderland now head to the Midlands seeking to end a seven-game winless run away against Aston Villa across all competitions (D3 L4), with their last victory at Villa Park coming in January 2011 when Phil Bardsley’s late strike secured a 1-0 Premier League triumph under Steve Bruce.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana – who signed a contract extension earlier this week – and Matteo Ruggeri both remain sidelined through injury, while Matty Cash is also out after picking up concussion on international duty with Poland.

Industry observers note that however, Johan Manzambi is available for selection after recovering from a calf issue, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka should also be ready to play after missing the last six games with a thigh injury. He could therefore compete with Taylor Harwood-Bellis for the right-back berth.

According to recent reports, nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and Alysson were all on the scoresheet at Old Trafford and will hope to retain their starting spots in the final third. Leon Goretzka also scored against Man United but he faces competition from Joao Gomes to start in centre-midfield alongside Boubacar Kamara.

As for Sunderland, Le Bris has confirmed that captain Granit Xhaka (calf) and striker Brian Brobbey (thigh) are ruled out due to injury, joining Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard and Habib Diarra (both thigh) in the treatment room.

However, Omar Alderete is back from a one-match suspension and could replace Luke O'Nein at centre-back, joining Trai Hume, Nordi Mukiele and Reinildo Mandava in defence.

Chemsdine Talbi was handed his first PL start of the season against Chelsea and will hope to continue on the left flank ahead of Nilson Angulo, while Wilson Isidor – who scored home and away against Villa last season – is set to lead the line in Brobbey's absence.

Aston Villa possible starting lineup:.

Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Goretzka; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson.

Sunderland possible starting lineup:.

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, Alderete, Reinildo; Ahoka, Sadiki; Meunier, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor.

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

While the Black Cats will be desperate to build on their victory over Chelsea as they bid to climb away from danger, the absence of both Xhaka and Brobbey is a real blow, and we expect Villa to ultimately navigate their way to a narrow triumph on home soil.

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick as head coach following a disastrous start to the 2026/27 campaign that has left the club in the Premier League relegation zone.

The former Manchester United midfielder was informed of the decision today after travelling to the Carrington after meeting chief executive Omar Berrada, director of football Jason Wilcox and co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Recent findings suggest that michael Carrick initially took charge on an interim basis after Ruben Amorim was sacked last season. He had a great start in the interim role, guiding Manchester United to third place and securing a return to the Champions League after missing the last two seasons.

His first full season at Old Trafford has been a completely different story.

Manchester United have managed just one Premier League victory from their opening 10 matches, collecting just eight points from five draws and four defeats. Their only win came against Ipswich Town in August, while a disastrous run of results has pushed the club down to 18th in the table.

Sunday’s chaotic late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa was another setback, with United failing to climb out of the relegation zone before the international break.

Manchester United have already identified Mauricio Pochettino as their preferred replacement, with reports indicating that an agreement in principle has been reached with the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager.

The Argentine is right now in charge of the United States national team but is understood to be interested in taking the Old Trafford job.

Recent findings suggest that pochettino’s contract reportedly includes a release clause worth around £7-7.5 million, which United would need to activate. Talks over personal terms are also understood to be advanced with Pochettino’s camp.

United are now preparing for another change in the dugout, with Pochettino expected to be handed the responsibility of rescuing their season.

“Quite simply disgusting”: Gary Neville tears into Manchester United over Carrick sacking

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Gary Neville has released a furious attack on Manchester United’s leadership over the way the club handled Michael Carrick’s dismissal.
  • United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.
  • The club stated it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gary Neville has released a furious attack on Manchester United’s leadership over the way the club handled Michael Carrick’s dismissal.

United confirmed on Thursday that Carrick had been sacked, four days after the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa left them 18th in the Premier League with eight points from 10 games.

The club stated it had reached the “extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary”.

Neville had already branded the process “classless” on The Overlap’s Stick to Football podcast before the announcement, pointing out that it was widely known Carrick was about to go while United were holding talks with potential replacements.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the decision was confirmed, the former United captain went even further.

“It’s just quite simply disgusting,” he said.

It has been revealed that “That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.”.

Neville took particular aim at the decision to hold the crucial meeting in Monaco, with chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flying out to meet Sir Jim Ratcliffe while Carrick was still taking training at Carrington.

“The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership,” he mentioned.

In a recent development, it seems the only ones not to realise that are the trio above, but they aren’t stupid. How they explain it, or attempt to rationalise, it will be painful to listen to.

It has been revealed that neville also argued the club should have acted sooner. Looking back to the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth in October, he said United “effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch” as he waved goodbye to supporters at full time, only for the board to hand him three more games.

He summed up the episode as “indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership”.

It’s more than an episode, it’s an omnishambles that reflects the dysfunctional state of MUFC in its current guise.

United are now expected to move promptly for Mauricio Pochettino. The United States head coach is reported to have reached an agreement in principle with the club, which is prepared to pay his release clause.

First, they will need to wait until the USMNT completes its CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

According to recent reports, yes. Man United to wait until an international break to appoint an international manager….

For Neville, though, the bigger problem lies above the dugout and no manager can be the scapegoat for that massive matter.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have confirmed an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, with the Argentine set to take charge after the international break.
  • It has been revealed that the 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was dismissed on Thursday following United’s disastrous start to the Premier League season.
  • The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is right now managing the United States national team but is expected to fly straight to Manchester after completing his USA international games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have confirmed an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, with the Argentine set to take charge after the international break.

It has been revealed that the 54-year-old will replace Michael Carrick, who was dismissed on Thursday following United’s disastrous start to the Premier League season. Pochettino is set to sign a two-and-a-half-year contract that will keep him at Old Trafford until the summer of 2029.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss is right now managing the United States national team but is expected to fly straight to Manchester after completing his USA international games.

Pochettino will first oversee the USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final ties against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday. He is expected to arrive in Manchester on Wednesday before taking charge of the club on Thursday.

Pochettino’s first taste of action as a United manager will be against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

Pochettino brings considerable Premier League experience after previous spells with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. He has also managed Paris Saint-Germain before the USA job.

His appointment makes him Manchester United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

Carrick’s departure came less than six months after he signed a two-year contract. His second spell in charge ended after United managed just one win in their opening 10 league matches, leaving them in the relegation zone.

Carrick’s coaching staff, including Jonny Evans, Jonathan Woodgate, Steve Holland, Travis Binnion and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson, have all left alongside Carrick.

  • The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13.

In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.

The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.

Blackpool return to action on Saturday fresh off the dismissal of manager Evatt with the hopes of climbing away from the League One drop zone.

They endured a tough start to their first full campaign under Evatt, right now sitting 20th with just 12 points on the board from 13 games, winning three and losing seven of those.

The most recent of those victories came in October to end a six-game winless run in the third tier, but the Tangerines failed to build on it, going on to lose 4-1 to Mansfield and rescue a 1-1 draw against a Sheffield Wednesday side who played the second half with 10 men.

Then after scraping past non-league AFC Hornchurch in extra time in the FA Cup first round, they visited AFC Wimbledon last weekend and again came away empty-handed, having failed to find a leveller after Alistair Smith's 13th-minute.

That triggered the dismissal of Evatt by the club hierarchy on Thursday, and now under the temporary charge of Steve Thompson and only above the relegation zone on goal difference, they will be desperate to begin rebuilding confidence and a cushion over the bottom four with a much-needed home win.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to continue an upturn in form and their climb away from the relegation zone.

Wigan Athletic also endured a tough start to their League One campaign under Gary Caldwell, sitting bottom after 12 games with just seven points on the board having lost nine of those matches.

That was largely down to the Latics' struggles in attack, but they appear to have turned a corner since, winning two and drawing one of their last three league games while scoring five goals, firstly ending a three-game losing run by beating fellow strugglers Bromley 3-2.

Then following a stalemate with Mansfield Town and consecutive cup wins over Boreham Wood and Crewe Alexandra, Caldwell's men went into another important contest at home to Barnsley on Saturday and won 2-1 as Fraser Murray put them ahead, Cameron McGeehan pegged them back and Jensen Weir scored the decisive goal 15 minutes from time.

Still with plenty of cause for concern in their away record, having drawn one and lost six of seven league games on the road, but finally with some momentum on their side, Wigan Athletic head to Bloomfield Road in search of a third win in four games to build on their two-point lead over the drop zone.

Blackpool were hit by a sickness bug for last weekend's game, with Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe among those to miss out.

They may be back in contention for Saturday, while defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe remain sidelined alongside George Honeyman.

Karoy Anderson will head back from international duty with Jamaica but was in action in Mexico on Wednesday, while Dion Charles, Jerry Yates, CJ Hamilton and Niall Ennis will all compete for attacking places after Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham partnered up up top last time out.

Wigan Athletic will likely remain without forwards Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris due to ongoing injuries.

Scott Hogan is back in contention after a brief layoff and came off the bench last time out, but Caldwell may go unchanged from the Barnsley win, with Christian Saydee leading the line with support from Bradley Burrowes and Jon Mellish.

Murray will continue to offer attacking support in a wing-back role after his opener against Barnsley, while Weir and Max Power will continue in the middle of a 3-4-3 setup.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Southwood; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Niskanen, Morgan, Brown, Coulson; Bowler, Charles, Yates.

Wigan Athletic possible starting lineup:.

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, Murray; Burrowes, Mellish; Saydee.

Blackpool remain devoid of confidence and have been hit by injuries, illness and a managerial departure, but they still have more quality than their league standing suggests while the visitors have been poor away from home this season.

We see the Tangerines at least avoiding defeat against a resurgent Wigan team.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:05 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 18:02 EST, 15 November 2026.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel.

The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order.

There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing.

‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ noted the head coach.

Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and said: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’.

It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain.

James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order.

According to recent reports, branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner.

Industry observers note that everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions.

Industry observers note that for King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino officially begins work as United head coach on Wednesday, just four days before his first match against Liverpool at Anfield.

The 54-year-old replaces Michael Carrick, who was dismissed last week after United won just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them 18th in the table.

Pochettino arrives after completing his final assignment with the United States, who beat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday to secure an 8-0 aggregate victory in their CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

The Argentine has signed a contract until the summer of 2029 and is expected to meet his new players and oversee his first training session on Thursday.

Speaking after his final match with the United States, Pochettino acknowledged the challenge awaiting him in Manchester.

“The new challenge is a significant challenge, but at the same time it’s adrenaline you want to feel,” he mentioned.

Several members of his coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez, travelled to Manchester earlier this week to begin preparations. Pochettino will have limited time to work with his squad before Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Liverpool, which kicks off at 4.30pm GMT.

The former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager inherits a United side struggling for results after a difficult opening to the campaign. He previously guided Tottenham to the 2019 Champions League final and won the French league title during his spell with Paris Saint-Germain.

United’s next fixtures also include a Champions League trip to Sporting CP and a home Premier League match against Brentford. Pochettino’s immediate task is to improve United’s league position, beginning with a demanding first match at Anfield.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ecuador’s late World Cup surge has given Chelsea a useful development signal through Moises Caicedo and Kendry Paez before Xabi Alonso’s first pre-season friendly on 28 July.

Chelsea confirmed that Caicedo and Paez reached the Round of 32 after Ecuador’s dramatic 2-1 win over Germany.

For Alonso, the contrast between the two Chelsea midfielders matters as much as the result.

Caicedo captained Ecuador through the pressure game, with We Ain’t Got No History highlighting the Chelsea midfielder’s leadership role in a win that rescued their tournament.

Paez, meanwhile, sits in a different phase of his rise.

Industry observers note that that should not worry Chelsea. FIFA identified Paez as one of the tournament’s wonderkids, but Chelsea’s bigger win is that he can absorb elite-tournament preparation without carrying a defining role too soon.

Read Chelsea has already looked at how Alonso must handle Paez’s development curve, and this knockout place sharpens that argument.

Alonso inherits a midfield loaded with senior names, transfer noise and immediate pressure.

Sources indicate that caicedo gives Chelsea the proven pillar. Paez gives them the controlled upside.

Ecuador’s run now gives Chelsea both at once.

For Chelsea, that is the ideal succession picture: leadership today, patience for tomorrow.
